_comment: Reading conventions for the Tehilim pages, consumed by tools/tehilim-build.mjs. These exist because the transliteration engine romanises what is WRITTEN, while a page teaches what is SAID. Every entry here was read off the ten pages that already shipped, not chosen afresh: `a-do-NAY` for the Tetragrammaton appears 47 times across them and zero pages read it letter by letter.

readAs._comment: Vocalized Hebrew -> the transliteration a reader should say. Keyed on the exact consonant+vowel string as it comes out of the Masoretic text, both spellings of the divine name included because MAM uses each.

defaultGloss._comment: Glosses so fixed that leaving them to an author would only introduce variation. Everything else is authored per verse, in context.

page._comment: Fixed strings the pages share. `tehilimWord` is the vocalized spelling used in every subtitle; the psalm's Hebrew numeral comes from Sefaria's own heRef, never computed here.

attribution._comment: Printed on every generated page. The Hebrew is share-alike and the English is public domain; saying so is the condition on which both may be used.
attribution.hebrew: Hebrew text: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), after the Aleppo Codex, via Sefaria, CC BY-SA.
attribution.english: English: The Holy Scriptures, a New Translation (JPS 1917), via Sefaria, public domain.
attribution.transliteration: Transliteration generated by this site's own engine (assets/translit.js).

pardesLevels._comment: The four PARDES headings are identical on every page, so they live here rather than in each authored file. An author picks a level by key and writes only the body; that also keeps Hebrew out of the authored content, which tools/tehilim-validate.mjs enforces.
